 Odisha raises DA to 63% bringing relief for employees and pensioners
 A 3% increase in DA and DR will benefit 8.5 lakh state employees and pensioners; revised payouts will be effective from 1 July. By Liji Narayan | HRKatha November 18, 2026 2 Mins Read 1050 Views

 In a move that will boost take-home earnings for government staff, the Odisha government has approved a three per cent increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for its employees. With this revision, the DA rate has risen from 60 per cent to 63 per cent of basic pay.
 The enhancement will take effect retrospectively from 1 July, ensuring that employees receive the benefit for the intervening months as well. The revised allowance will be paid in cash along with salaries for November, according to an official statement issued by the Chief Minister’s Office.
 The decision extends beyond serving employees. Pensioners in the state will also see their Dearness Relief (DR) rise by three per cent, providing additional support against the impact of inflation and rising living costs.
 The latest revision is expected to benefit approximately 8.5 lakh Odisha government employees and pensioners collectively, offering a significant financial cushion at a time when household expenses continue to remain elevated.
 The announcement follows a similar decision by the Union government last month. The Centre approved an additional three per cent DA and DR instalment for Central government employees and pensioners with effect from 1 July, 2026, raising the rate from 60 per cent to 63 per cent. The increase was intended to offset the effects of inflation and was implemented in line with the formula recommended by the 7th Central Pay Commission.
 The move reflects the continuing role of DA and DR adjustments as key instruments for maintaining employee purchasing power, supporting financial wellbeing and reinforcing compensation competitiveness amid changing economic conditions.
